module purpose: neorv32_cpu_cp_fpu decodes floating-point control fields, captures operands, operand classes and rounding mode, executes classification, comparison, sign-injection, min/max, integer/float conversion, add/sub and multiply paths, and returns a result word with a valid indication. It also stores CSR rounding mode and accrued exception flags, and reads those CSRs back on csr_rdata_o.

use-case flows.value: CSR rounding mode and accrued exception-flag state written from csr_wdata_i
decode a supported FPU instruction and latch operation kind, operands, operand classes, compare condition and effective rounding mode
compute classify, compare, sign-injection and min/max results and flags
compute integer/float conversions, multiply, add/subtract and normalization results and flags
selected result word, selected per-operation exception flags, and completion-valid indication
read back accrued exception flags, rounding mode, or combined fcsr on csr_rdata_o
clear CSR state, latched operation context, FU state, result and current flags when rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.concept: Effective rounding mode used by an FPU operation
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores the CSR rounding mode in csr_frm from csr_wdata_i at lines 286-292. The operate flow then captures the effective mode in fpu_operands.frm: from csr_frm when ctrl_i.ir_funct3 = "111" (430), otherwise from the instruction field itself (432). That stored mode is consumed by the f2i and normalizer sub-units at lines 697 and 1465 and by add/sub zero-sign handling at lines 1156-1159 and 1175-1178. Integrity is established because changing this value changes the implemented rounding behavior and result selection; availability is established by CSR readback at lines 306-307 and by holding the mode between capture and use.

The module stores accrued exception status in csr_fflags. CSR writes can set it directly at lines 282-283 and 290-292, while the non-write path accumulates new flags with `csr_fflags <= csr_fflags or fflags` at line 295. The read-out flow returns it on csr_rdata_o at lines 305 and 307. Integrity is established because software-visible exception status must follow these write and accumulation rules; availability is established because the register holds state between writes and is returned by the read flow.

conceptual assets.concept: Latched operation control context for the current FPU instruction
conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 316-340 decode the control fields into one supported operation class, line 425 stores the selected operation code in funct_ff, and lines 1419-1447 and 1496-1514 use funct_ff to select the normalizer inputs and the result/flag source. Line 426 stores cmp_i in cmp_ff, and lines 513-523 and 549-570 use cmp_ff to derive comparison behavior. Integrity is established because corrupting this stored control context misroutes which computation runs and which result or flags are reported. Availability is established because the context is captured in S_IDLE and held until completion.

conceptual assets.concept: Latched operand values and operand-class information for the current operation
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operand path forms internal operand words from rs1_i and rs2_i at lines 347-353, classifies both operands at lines 358-396, and stores the operand words and their classes in fpu_operands.rs1, fpu_operands.rs2, fpu_operands.rs1_class and fpu_operands.rs2_class at lines 437-440. Those stored values then drive classify output (485), compare/minmax logic (503-678), sign injection (716-726), the f2i sub-unit inputs (700-703), and multiplier/add-sub/normalizer inputs (785-851, 1065-1439). Integrity is established because all implemented arithmetic and exception cases depend on these stored values; availability is established because they are held after issue until the operation completes.

conceptual assets.concept: Completion-valid event for an issued FPU operation
conceptual assets.reasoning: In S_BUSY, line 448 tests whether the active functional path is done or a CPU trap occurs; line 449 sets ctrl_engine.valid and line 450 returns the control engine to S_IDLE. Line 462 exports that event on valid_o, and line 1495 uses the same stored event to gate result and current-flag capture. Integrity is established because consumers must observe completion exactly under these implemented conditions; availability is established whenever the done-or-trap condition occurs.

The module computes branch-specific results for classify (485-486), compare (597-620), sign-injection (715-727), min/max (673-677), f2i through the sub-unit output at line 705, and add/sub, multiply and i2f through the normalizer path selected at lines 1419-1447 and received at line 1475. When ctrl_engine.valid is asserted, output_gate selects the source according to funct_ff and registers the selected value onto res_o at lines 1495-1514. Integrity is established because the external consumer must receive the result defined by the selected operation and completion event; availability is established under that valid condition.

When ctrl_engine.valid is asserted, output_gate selects the flags belonging to the completed operation into fflags at lines 1495-1514. The CSR-update flow later consumes that stored value in `csr_fflags <= csr_fflags or fflags` when csr_we_i = '0' (295). Integrity is established because exception reporting and accumulation depend on the exact selected flag set; availability is established for the implemented path that latches flags on completion and accumulates them on a later non-CSR-write cycle.
